production_changes: On-screen fill order uses world-space distance to the viewport center, with stable input-order ties. Off-screen viewport-distance and row-order pacing remains unchanged.

ProgressiveSurface ranks the full eligible missing-tile queue by uncovered pixels before selecting the existing 4/32-tile batches. The submit-time residency/dedupe check and preparation guard remain intact.
new_regression_cases: Production center-out geometry is not reset to top-left row order; exact center-distance ties retain input order.
The final uncovered tile in a 36-tile plan advances to the first batch for both 4- and 32-tile batch sizes; all 36 tiles are submitted exactly once.
A lower-density preview covering the entire viewport and a frame without pixels both preserve center-first native scheduling.
Shared preparation viewport still covers the full visible plan, including transport gutters, after gap-first reordering.
One hundred superseding pan/resize updates keep only the latest successor and reuse the four in-flight tiles that become ready, yielding each of 36 tile keys exactly once.
scope_limits: Tests execute production scheduling and surface orchestration on CPU with controllable worker transport; default suites additionally initialize the existing production WASM planner.
No real GPU pixel, frame-rate, or GPU-residency measurement is claimed.
Product GPU defaults, tile identities, sampling phase, native render scale, visibility certification, masks/effect execution, off-screen pacing, and cancellation ownership are unchanged.
compatibility_note: Existing scheduler assertions that explicitly pinned visible row order were updated for the intentional center-priority policy. Two low-zoom surface tests now assert the full tile set rather than unrelated row order; prefetch and cancellation checks are retained.
